διότι δὲ πολιτικὸν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ζῷον πάσης μελίττης καὶ παντὸς ἀγελαίου ζῴου μᾶλλον, δῆλον. οὐθὲν γάρ, ὡς φαμέν, μάτην ἡ φύσις ποιεῖ· λόγον δὲ μόνον ἄνθρωπος ἔχει τῶν ζῴων·
ἡ μὲν οὖν φωνὴ τοῦ λυπηροῦ καὶ ἡδέος ἐστὶ σημεῖον, διὸ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις ὑπάρχει ζῴοις· μέχρι γὰρ τούτου ἡ φύσις αὐτῶν ἐλήλυθε, τοῦ ἔχειν αἴσθησιν λυπηροῦ καὶ ἡδέος καὶ ταῦτα σημαίνειν ἀλλήλοις·
ὁ δὲ λόγος ἐπὶ τῷ δηλοῦν ἐστι τὸ συμφέρον καὶ τὸ βλαβερόν, ὥστε καὶ τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὸ ἄδικον· τοῦτο γὰρ πρὸς τὰ ἄλλα ζῷα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἴδιον, τὸ μόνον ἀγαθοῦ καὶ κακοῦ καὶ δικαίου καὶ ἀδίκου καὶ τῶν ἄλλων αἴσθησιν ἔχειν· ἡ δὲ τούτων κοινωνία ποιεῖ οἰκίαν καὶ πόλιν.

ἡ μὲν οὖν φωνὴ τοῦ λυπηροῦ καὶ ἡδέος ἐστὶ σημεῖον, διὸ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις ὑπάρχει ζῴοις· μέχρι γὰρ τούτου ἡ φύσις αὐτῶν ἐλήλυθε, τοῦ ἔχειν αἴσθησιν λυπηροῦ καὶ ἡδέος καὶ ταῦτα σημαίνειν ἀλλήλοις·
ὁ δὲ λόγος ἐπὶ τῷ δηλοῦν ἐστι τὸ συμφέρον καὶ τὸ βλαβερόν, ὥστε καὶ τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὸ ἄδικον· τοῦτο γὰρ πρὸς τὰ ἄλλα ζῷα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἴδιον, τὸ μόνον ἀγαθοῦ καὶ κακοῦ καὶ δικαίου καὶ ἀδίκου καὶ τῶν ἄλλων αἴσθησιν ἔχειν· ἡ δὲ τούτων κοινωνία ποιεῖ οἰκίαν καὶ πόλιν.
analysis.literalTranslation:
That the human being is a political animal more than any bee and any gregarious animal is evident. For nature, as we say, does nothing in vain; and among the animals the human being alone has speech.
Voice, then, on the one hand, is a sign of the painful and the pleasant, and therefore it also belongs to the other animals; for their nature has advanced up to this point: to have perception of the painful and the pleasant and to signify these things to one another.
But speech is for making clear the advantageous and the harmful, and so also the just and the unjust; for this is peculiar to human beings in relation to the other animals: alone to have perception of good and bad and just and unjust and the other things; and the sharing of these things makes a household and a city.
analysis.naturalTranslation:
It is evident that a human being is more fully a political animal than any bee or any other gregarious animal. Nature, as we say, does nothing in vain: human beings alone among animals possess rational speech.
Voice is a sign of pleasure and pain, and for that reason other animals possess it too; their nature has developed far enough to perceive pleasure and pain and communicate these to one another.
Rational speech, however, serves to disclose what is advantageous and harmful, and therefore what is just and unjust. This is distinctive of human beings in relation to other animals: they alone can perceive good and bad, justice and injustice, and other such things. Sharing these judgments is what constitutes a household and a city.

tokens.morphology: Pres. Act. Part. Acc. Sg. n.

notes.text: Here διότι introduces the proposition whose truth is predicated by the following impersonal δῆλον; it is therefore best taken as content 'that', not causal 'because'.
μᾶλλον takes the genitives πάσης μελίττης and παντὸς ἀγελαίου ζῴου as genitives of comparison.

Although μόνον is formally compatible with an accusative singular masculine adjective agreeing with λόγον, the syntax and argument require adverbial 'alone': the human being alone among animals possesses λόγος.
The genitive article introduces an epexegetical articular infinitive dependent on τούτου: the point reached is the capacity to perceive pain and pleasure and to signal them.

The δέ preceding λόγος answers the earlier μέν and establishes a conceptual contrast between φωνή, voice as a sign of pleasure and pain, and λόγος, articulate or rational speech capable of expressing evaluative distinctions.
ἐπί with the dative articular infinitive expresses function or purpose: λόγος exists 'for making clear' the distinctions that follow.
ὥστε introduces an elliptical continuation of δηλοῦν: speech thereby also makes clear the just and the unjust.
The nominative neuter article introduces an articular infinitive phrase in apposition to τοῦτο, specifying what is ἴδιον to human beings.

τούτων gathers the preceding objects of human perception—good and bad, just and unjust, and related values—and κοινωνία denotes participation or sharing in them, which is said to constitute household and polis.
